sections.content:
56,335 people

were counted on the census as "medical secretaries" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Medical secretaries deal with correspondence, make appointments, handle patients� queries, file and maintain medical records and other records, and perform other clerical tasks in hospitals, surgeries and other medical establishments.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "medical secretaries" there were more women than men (95.4% compared with 4.6%).

This means "medical secretaries" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "secretarial and related occupations".

Men made up 4.6% and women made up 95.4% of "medical secretaries"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "medical secretaries" included:

  • school midday and crossing patrol occupations
  • registered community nurses
  • childminders

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "medical secretaries" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "medical secretaries", 17.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "medical secretaries" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "medical secretaries" included:

  • elementary cleaning occupations (other)
  • market and street traders and assistants
  • library clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "medical secretaries" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of women than men with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "medical secretaries" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "medical secretaries", 12.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (54.4% compared with 45.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.5%) than self-employed (2.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
